attacks.attack: The acceptance law's scale-adaptation claim is arithmetically backwards. DeltaL_perc as specified (Huber-mean over AFFECTED TILES + probe residual sum) grows with the number of boundary pixels an edit touches, while DeltaMDL is a fixed integer (~30-40 bits per parameter shared). So a mirror-symmetry edit spending 1.3px on a 400px logo touches thousands of boundary pixels and accumulates a huge Lab/probe cost against a constant MDL bonus — it FAILS, the exact opposite of the design's stated behavior ('a 1.3px cost on a 400px logo passes'). Flip to mean-normalization and the opposite failure appears: a locally destructive edit on a small feature of a big shape gets diluted to invisibility and passes. Either normalization choice breaks one end; the single-knob lambda_mdl calibrated on 365 logos will silently encode whichever pathology the corpus underrepresents. This is the central mechanism of the whole design, so as written it either never idealizes large art or vandalizes small features of large shapes.
attacks.fix: Price both sides in the same units: DeltaL_perc = per-boundary-sample JND-normalized residual (mean Huber per probe, weighted by sigma_i), and make DeltaMDL scale with the evidence count it governs (bits saved per boundary sample), i.e. accept iff mean_perceptual_cost_per_probe <= lambda * bits_saved_per_probe + tau. Add a separate absolute cap on max local residual (already half-present as the probe veto) so mean-dilution can't hide local damage. Validate the law on a synthetic scale-sweep (same logo rendered at 24/64/256/512px) before any corpus calibration.

attacks.attack: Stage 0 declares linear-RGB unmixing 'non-negotiable' because 'coverage is linear in light' — but the majority of real-world flat art is anti-aliased in sRGB GAMMA space (Skia/Chrome, Cairo, GDI+, most icon exporters composite without linear blending). For those inputs, converting to linear and inverting an erf ESF introduces exactly the systematic 0.15px-class edge bias the design claims to eliminate, worst on high-contrast dark/light edges (i.e., text). The advertised 0.03-0.08px probe accuracy is then unreachable, and the downstream ±0.15px 'shrunken corridors' become confidently WRONG corridors: the DP is over-constrained around biased probes, Algorithm-1 repair churns, and shapes land on the fallback ladder precisely on clean inputs where the design promises its biggest win.
attacks.fix: Make blending-space a calibrated per-image parameter, not an axiom: fit the erf ESF to straight-edge profiles in BOTH linear and sRGB space (and one intermediate gamma), pick the space with lower profile residual, and do all unmixing/render-comparison in that same space (bias cancels when analysis and synthesis share the space). ~1 day of work; also fixes re-encoded/Photoshop-exported assets with odd transfer curves.

attacks.attack: Alpha saturation and aliased input break the evidence field. ESF^-1 is only invertible for |d| ≲ 1.5w (~0.7px at w=0.45): (a) when ICM/Potts labeling puts the crack a full pixel off the true edge (documented behavior of Potts smoothing on thin features), alpha saturates at 0/1 and the probe silently clamps at the saturation boundary while still carrying small sigma — a tight corridor around a fabricated position; (b) on non-anti-aliased input (pixel art, hard-thresholded scans, many favicon-size assets) alpha is binary everywhere, ESF calibration drives w→0 making ESF^-1 divide-by-zero ill-conditioned, and the entire coverage-as-evidence premise evaporates — yet Stages 2-6 all assume probes exist. The design has no stated behavior for its evidence channel being empty.
attacks.fix: Two guards: (1) sigma_i = inf whenever alpha_obs is outside [0.05, 0.95] or the fitted w < 0.15px, so saturated/aliased pixels degrade to the current ±0.5px midpoint corridor instead of lying confidently; (2) an explicit input-regime switch: if the fraction of informative boundary alphas is below a floor, run the pipeline in 'no-evidence mode' (midpoint corridors, template fits scored on binary coverage, court still works — it just has coarser testimony). Both are cheap because the corridor formula ±max(0.5, 2sigma_i) already degrades gracefully once sigma is honest.

attacks.attack: Thin strokes and small text — the headline use case — violate the two-color unmixing model in a circular way. A 1-2px stroke has zero pixels '>=1px from any boundary', so (a) the interior-median color re-estimation is undefined, and (b) the unmixing endpoint A (stroke color) is never observed pure — every observed pixel is already a mixture, so the palette anchor for small glyphs is AA-desaturated. Unmixing against a wrong endpoint biases every alpha, hence every probe, on exactly the features the design claims to win. Additionally opposite edges of a 1px stroke share pixels, so per-edge alpha is a sum of two coverages and the single-line half-plane check inflates sigma everywhere along the stroke — small text ends up with the WORST evidence in the image, not the best.
attacks.fix: For features whose distance-transform ridge < 1.5px, estimate color and geometry jointly instead of sequentially: use the existing stroke detector's centerline, model each pixel as c = alpha_total*A + (1-alpha_total)*B with alpha_total from a two-edge (width, offset) coverage model, and solve for (A, width, centerline offset) by least squares along the run. Same machinery the template league already needs; reuse its analytic-coverage fitter with a 'capsule/stroke' template.

attacks.attack: The hard probe veto (>2% of sigma<0.15px probes moved >1.5px) is scale-blind in the wrong direction. On a 24px icon, 1.5px is 6% of the canvas — intentional micro-asymmetries (italic slant, optical overshoot in professional logotypes, deliberately unequal counters) move probes well under 1.5px and get flattened by high-MDL symmetry edits: the system 'idealizes' away brand-accurate design, the exact over-idealization failure the veto exists to stop. On a 500px logo, 1.5px is invisible and the veto fires on harmless idealizations. Also note the veto only consults sigma<0.15px probes, which per the JPEG numbers (0.2-0.4px) means the veto is entirely INACTIVE on JPEG input — no bound on idealization at all for the most common file format.
attacks.fix: Make the veto threshold max(0.5px, 1.5% of shape extent), test signed-residual COHERENCE (a contiguous arc of same-sign residuals = deliberate asymmetry) rather than a raw count, and define the veto over the best-available probes per shape (top confidence quantile) instead of an absolute sigma cutoff so it never silently disables itself on JPEG.

attacks.attack: Template league as specified is unbuildable: 'alpha_pred is the template's exact pixel coverage (analytic for these primitives)' is false for superellipse, star, cross, and rotated N-gon — superellipse pixel coverage has no closed form, and none of these are analytically differentiable in their shape parameters for the 30-step Adam fit. Separately, the coverage-residual loss over 3-7 params including theta is multimodal (rotated-square-vs-diamond, rounded-rect-vs-capsule basins), and 30 Adam steps from one init routinely lands in the wrong basin — on a 6x6 shape the wrong template can still score decently, and the MDL bonus then locks in a WRONG idealization (a diamond shipped as a rotated square) that survives the court because both render within tau_floor at that size.
attacks.fix: Replace 'exact analytic coverage' with a smooth signed-distance-field coverage surrogate alpha = ESF(sdf(p; params)) evaluated on a 3x3-supersampled grid — differentiable for every template in the league, one implementation for all. Fight multimodality with cheap multi-start (4 orientations + moment-based init) and let ALL converged candidates enter the court rather than pre-picking; ambiguity at sizes where the render can't distinguish should be broken by a fixed template-prior order (deterministic tie-break), documented in the audit.

attacks.attack: Painter's-stack depth inference meets genuinely cyclic flat art far more often than 'rare': interlocking rings (Olympics, Audi), chain-link logos, and woven/knot marks are staple logo motifs where A overlaps B overlaps A. The design punts to 'per-neighborhood partition fallback', but that fallback reintroduces the seam class the stack was built to abolish, precisely on high-profile logos. Second mechanism-level hole: '+0.75px inflation along that interface only' creates outline discontinuities where a shape's boundary transitions from a losing interface to a winning one — the inflated segment ends 0.75px off the un-inflated continuation, producing a self-intersection or a poke-out sliver at exactly the junctions where three regions meet, visible as a colored nick at 4x (the audit's own seam scan will catch it, but the design contains no repair).
attacks.fix: Cycles: break them by splitting ONE shape into two sub-paths at its narrowest occluded waist (the standard interlocking-rings SVG idiom — VAI does this), which keeps the stack invariant instead of abandoning it. Inflation: taper the offset smoothly to zero over ~2px approaching any interface endpoint/junction, and clip the inflated outline against the winner's path; both are local polyline operations on geometry that is never visible.

attacks.attack: Fallback rung 4 fails its two stated jobs simultaneously. A single closed cubic B-spline cannot represent corners, so any glyph or shape that reaches rung 4 (which happens most on messy input) gets serifs, stems, and terminals visibly rounded — text falling to the terminal rung ships blob-letters, arguably worse-than-VAI, the exact criterion under attack. Meanwhile n = perimeter/3 control points (100 CPs for a 300px loop) optimized against L_perc on JPEG input has enough freedom to chase ringing halos, reintroducing wobble; the FAIR epsilon that must simultaneously suppress this and not round real features is a single global constant tuned on clean data, and there is no per-image rule given for it.
attacks.fix: Make rung 4 a piecewise spline split at the surviving high-probability corner hypotheses (they exist — the CNN superset at 0.15 is already computed), C2 inside pieces, G0 at splits. Set the FAIR weight from measured noise: epsilon proportional to sigma_n^2 (and to the JPEG ringing amplitude estimate from Stage 0), so smoothing strength automatically rises on dirty input. Cap CP count at perimeter/6 with knot insertion only where probe residual demands it.

attacks.attack: The 'attack F1 from the decision side' story caps out below the Stage D gate. Shallow perceptual corners (obtuse ~150-165 deg, e.g. the near-flat vertices of wide letterforms and 7-segment-style logos) change tile coverage by less than tau_floor when removed — the render genuinely cannot see them — yet the Hoshyari human GT labels them, because humans infer them from context and repetition. For these events the court is structurally indifferent, the CNN at threshold 0.15 has mediocre precision, and mu*(1-p_cnn) pricing just reproduces detector quality. Event-F1 >= 0.80 on the human GT is therefore not reachable by rendered evidence alone; Stage D blocks and the schedule stalls on a gate the mechanism cannot satisfy.
attacks.fix: Let regularity evidence vote on corners before the court closes: after repeat-unification and mirror detection, corners confirmed in ANY instance of a matched group (or mirrored partner) get their MDL_corner cost slashed for all instances — repetition aggregates the sub-threshold coverage evidence the single tile lacks. Cheap because the matching machinery already exists in Stage 5; also re-scope the Stage D gate to 'F1 >= 0.80 after Stage F regularities' rather than on the isolated DP.

attacks.attack: JPEG 4:2:0 chroma subsampling is unmodeled: on chroma-dominant edges (red/green, blue/orange boundaries with similar luma — common in flat logos) the chroma channels are stored at half resolution and interpolated, so the observed color mixture along the edge does not lie on the A-B segment used for unmixing; the projection yields alphas biased by up to a full pixel of edge position with NORMAL unmixing residual (the residual check looks orthogonal to the segment, but subsampling error is largely along it). Probes are confidently wrong in a spatially correlated band, the Huber does not help because the bias is coherent, and per-image erf-w calibration (done on the strongest = luma edges) does not transfer.
attacks.fix: Detect subsampling from the JPEG headers (free), then on chroma-dominant interfaces (||A-B|| mostly in Cb/Cr) either unmix on the luma channel alone when it carries any contrast, or inflate sigma by the chroma-interpolation error model (~0.5-1px). Per-channel ESF widths (Y vs Cb/Cr) in Stage 0 cover the rest; one extra fitted parameter.

attacks.attack: ESF calibration prerequisites fail on the design's showcase inputs: a 24-32px icon frequently has NO 'long straight high-contrast boundary run' for the Hough+erf fit (everything is curved or shorter than ~8px), so w is fit from a handful of samples with huge variance or not at all; a biased w rescales every ESF^-1 inversion, i.e., a multiplicative error on ALL probe offsets of that image. Same story for tau_floor: the 2x-render-then-ESF-downsample synthesis channel does not exactly match the unknown source rasterizer's filter, so even the ground-truth SVG scores nonzero — with tau_floor as a global constant, images whose model mismatch exceeds it get systematically under-idealized and vice versa.
attacks.fix: Bayesian shrinkage for w: prior w0=0.45 (lossless) / w0=f(JPEG quality), posterior weighted by sample count, so small icons fall back to the prior instead of a garbage fit. Calibrate tau_floor per image, not globally: render the CURRENT accepted program once and set tau_floor to its residual quantile — that measures this image's channel mismatch directly.

attacks.attack: Stage 6 constraint-manifold reparameterization assumes accepted regularities compose into a tree, but the court can accept OVERLAPPING groups: a segment that is simultaneously a member of a shared carrier line, one arm of a mirror pair whose axis is not aligned with the carrier, and an edge of a rect template. Hard substitution then has no consistent reduced parameterization (the mirror image of a carrier-bound segment must also lie on a second, implied carrier that was never accepted); naive implementation either crashes, silently drops constraints nondeterministically, or lets diffvg gradients tear the shape. The design never specifies a conflict-resolution rule, and this WILL occur on the 365-logo corpus (grids of mirrored rectangles are everywhere).
attacks.fix: At freeze time build the constraint graph and reduce it explicitly: process accepted regularities in descending DeltaMDL order, adding each only if it is compatible with the current reduction (compatibility = the implied parameter substitution is expressible; a plain rank/consistency check on the linearized constraint system); incompatible edits are returned to the court as rejected with a logged reason. Deterministic, debuggable, ~1 day.

attacks.attack: Grayscale and near-monochrome art breaks 3-way junction unmixing categorically: black/gray/white palettes are COLLINEAR in RGB, so barycentric unmixing against three region colors is rank-deficient at every 3-region junction, sigma=inf everywhere near junctions, and junction geometry is carried solely by the retained region_graph pinning — meaning the design's junction quality on monochrome logos (a huge fraction of wordmarks) is exactly today's quality while the surrounding pipeline now expects probe support that never arrives (e.g., depth-order T-junction inference keys on tangent continuation measured from probes).
attacks.fix: Detect collinear palettes and switch junction handling to a geometric prior: fit the two crossing interfaces' probe sets (which are 2-color and healthy away from the junction pixel) and extrapolate to their analytic intersection — the existing _corner_intersection/_intersect_supports code does precisely this; just route junction pinning through it and never rely on 3-way unmixing when the color simplex is degenerate.
